q: Under the ASH Lifesaving Rules, who keeps people out of the line of fire?
why: The rule reads both ways: keep yourself and others out of the line of fire. Seeing a man standing in it makes it your problem. (ASH — Lifesaving Rules)

q: Per the ASH, before working unescorted on the North Slope you must complete:
o: A site tour with your supervisor
NSTC Unescorted training and the North Slope Orientation
why: NSTC Unescorted (or NSTC-approved equivalent) plus the North Slope Orientation, before arrival at your assigned location. (ASH — General Safety Rules)

q: H2S in your breathing zone exceeds 10 ppm. The ASH requires:
why: Above 10 ppm in the breathing zone, appropriate respiratory protection is required — no exposure-time workaround. (ASH — H2S Standard)

q: Noise in your work area exceeds 100 dBA. Required hearing protection:
why: Over 82 dBA takes single protection; over 100 dBA takes double — plugs and muffs together. (ASH — Industrial Hygiene)

q: Outside work is scheduled and the wind is blowing past 40 mph. The ASH calls for:
o: A safety time out / task hazard assessment before proceeding
why: Wind over 40 mph triggers a safety time out and task hazard assessment for any scheduled outside work — the job gets re-looked before it proceeds. (ASH — High Wind Conditions)

q: At what fall exposure does the ASH require 100% continuous fall protection on construction work?
why: Fall potential greater than 6 feet means 100% continuous fall protection — guardrails, nets, or personal restraint/arrest. (ASH — Fall Protection)

q: Body belts in a personal fall arrest system are:
o: Not acceptable — full body harness required
why: Body belts are positioning devices only. Fall ARREST takes a full body harness, locking snap hooks, 5,000-lb rated hardware. (ASH — Fall Protection)

q: Ground disturbance deeper than what depth requires an Area Civil Work Request (ACWR)?
why: Anything past 12 inches needs an ACWR before digging — buried cables and pipelines don't announce themselves. And an ACWR expires in 90 days if work hasn't started. (ASH — Ground Disturbance Standard)

q: Per the ASH Lifesaving Rules, energy isolation means:
why: Verify isolation before work begins — verification, not assumption, is the rule. (ASH — Lifesaving Rules / Energy Isolation Standard)

q: Walking under a suspended load is:
o: Allowed if the operator sees you
why: Follow safe lifting operations and do not walk under a suspended load — a Lifesaving Rule with no exception clause. (ASH — Lifesaving Rules)

q: You need to bypass a safety device to finish a task. The ASH says:
o: Do it and log it at shift end
Obtain authorization BEFORE bypassing or defeating it
OK if it's back in service by shift change
Supervisors may bypass at their discretion
why: Authorization comes before bypassing, inhibiting, or defeating any safety protection device — that's a Lifesaving Rule. (ASH — Defeated Safety Devices Standard)

q: Entering a confined space requires:
o: A gas test within the last 24 hours
Two people minimum, no permit needed
why: Obtain authorization before entering a confined space — the Lifesaving Rule behind the full entry standard and permit. (ASH — Confined Space Entry Standard)

q: The ASH driving rule, in full:
o: Seat belt, no mobile phone, don't exceed speed limits
Seat belt and CB radio contact
why: All three, together: belt on, phone down, speed limits respected. (ASH — Lifesaving Rules / Vehicle Safety)

q: Your vehicle breaks down on a field road. Reflective triangles go:
o: 100 ft in front, 10 ft behind, 100 ft behind
why: 100 in front, 10 behind, 100 behind — and hold the triangle between you and traffic while placing it so drivers can see you. Then contact Security. (ASH — Disabled Vehicle)

q: Passing working heavy equipment on a field road, you slow to:
why: 15 mph past working heavy equipment; on public roads, posted limits govern. (ASH — Vehicle Safety)

q: Driving in the field requires what communication equipment?
o: Some form of two-way communication, radio-checked before departure
why: Two-way comms are required for field driving, and the radio check happens before you roll, not after you're stuck. (ASH — Vehicle Safety)

q: High-visibility clothing is worn:
o: As the outermost layer on the upper body outdoors
why: Outermost layer on the upper body while working outdoors — hi-vis under a jacket is hi-vis for nobody. (ASH — PPE)

q: A crew member is shivering hard, stumbling, slurring, and drowsy. That's:
why: Intense shivering, poor coordination, thick speech, drowsiness — hypothermia. It's insidious, and untreated it ends in collapse and death. (ASH — Cold Related Injuries)

q: Frostbitten skin that's gone numb and dead white gets treated by:
o: Transport to a medical facility as soon as possible
Covering it and finishing the shift
why: Transport as soon as possible to a medical facility — and watch your co-workers' faces, because they can't see their own. (ASH — Cold Related Injuries)

q: The ASH's best defense against cold injury:
o: Prioritize and limit outside work in extremes, plus correct PPE
why: Limit exposure during temperature and wind chill extremes and dress right — gauntlet gloves specifically, to close the wrist gap between jacket and glove. (ASH — Cold Weather Protection)

q: You find a ladder with a loose rung. The ASH says:
o: Tag it and use the good side
Report it and remove it from service immediately
Use it for light duty only
Note it for the next inspection
why: Defective ladders come out of service immediately — report to your supervisor. Never use a defective ladder. (ASH — Ladder Safety)

q: A fixed ladder installed after November 2018 extending more than 24 feet must have:
o: A personal fall arrest system or ladder safety system
why: Post-2018 installs over 24 feet: fall arrest system or ladder safety system — cages alone no longer qualify for new installs. (ASH — Ladder Safety)

q: Barricading a hazardous area requires:
o: The barricade PLUS a highly visible sign identifying the hazard
why: Erect the barricade AND post a visible sign naming the hazard — tape that doesn't say why is tape people duck under. (ASH — Barricade Guidelines)

q: A ladder must block a doorway to do the job. The ASH requires:
o: A sign on the far side of the door
Lock or block the adjacent door; if it's an emergency exit, the ladder stays continually attended
Nothing if the door opens away
why: Lock or block adjacent doors, and a ladder blocking an emergency exit is never left alone — leave the area, clear the exit path. (ASH — Ladder Safety)

q: An emergency vehicle comes up on you on a field road. You:
o: Speed up to clear the area
Pull over, stop, and yield until it passes
why: All traffic meeting or being overtaken by an emergency vehicle yields, pulls over, and STOPS until it's past. (ASH — Vehicle Safety)

q: How many Lifesaving Rules does the ASH define?
why: Nine: line of fire, permit to work, confined space, work at heights, lifting, energy isolation, ground disturbance, defeating safety devices, driving. (ASH - Lifesaving Rules)

q: Which of these is NOT one of the nine Lifesaving Rules?
why: Housekeeping matters, but the nine rules are the fatal-risk barriers. The other three are all on the list. (ASH - Lifesaving Rules)

q: The Permit To Work lifesaving rule says:
o: Obtain a valid work permit when required
Verbal approval from the operator suffices
Permits are for hot work only
why: A VALID permit, WHEN required - and the standards define when. Working past an expired permit breaks the same rule. (ASH - Lifesaving Rules)

q: To replace a valve you have to alter part of the system. Under the ASH fall-protection section, that work is classified as:
why: Alteration to a system to replace a valve is construction work under 1926 - which drives the 100% continuous fall protection requirement above 6 feet. (ASH - Fall Protection)

q: Riding in a vehicle on a gravel road, eye protection is:
o: Required unless Company policy exempts it
why: Gravel-road vehicle travel is on the eye-protection list unless the Company policy says otherwise. (ASH - PPE)

q: A hand is grinding 15 feet away from you with no welding screen up. Your eye protection:
o: The same level as the grinder - sealed eyewear and face shield
why: Within 20 feet of grinding, chipping, or blasting, you wear the same protection as the man doing it, unless barriers separate you. (ASH - PPE)

q: Which hard hat is banned on site?
why: Metal hard hats are not allowed. Class E to ANSI Z89.1 is the requirement; compliant climbing helmets are permitted. (ASH - PPE)

q: A worker with a goatee needs a tight-fitting respirator. The ASH says:
o: Facial hair that breaks the seal means no tight-fitting respirator
Use a nuisance dust mask instead
why: Goatees, large moustaches, and long sideburns interfere with the seal - and a respirator that does not seal is not protection. (ASH - PPE)

q: For workers at flash-fire risk, which fabric is prohibited unless rated for the exposure?
why: Acetate, nylon, polyester, and rayon - alone or in blends - are out unless rated for the conditions. They melt into the burn. (ASH - PPE)

q: Before reaching for a fall arrest harness, the ASH says first consider:
o: A fixed or mobile work platform with handrails
why: Where practical, a platform with handrails, mid-rails, and toe boards comes BEFORE a fall arrest system. Not falling beats falling well. (ASH - Fall Protection)

q: Personal fall arrest systems get a documented inspection:
o: At least annually by a qualified inspector, color coded
why: Visual check by the user before every use; documented annual inspection by a qualified inspector with color coding. Defective components come out of service. (ASH - Fall Protection)

q: Before starting work at height, tools and equipment must be:
o: Assessed for fall potential with controls in place
why: Assess the fall potential of everything you carry up, and control it - lanyards, positive securing, netting, screens. (ASH - Dropped Objects)

q: Below overhead work, the ASH requires:
o: An exclusion zone of suitable barriers
Nothing if hard hats are worn
why: An exclusion zone with barriers goes below overhead work - a hard hat is the last defense, not the plan. (ASH - Dropped Objects)

q: Working over water with drowning danger, a PFD is NOT required when:
o: 100% continuous fall protection prevents falling in
why: Coast Guard-approved PFD or buoyant vest - unless 100% fall protection makes falling in impossible. (ASH - Working Over or Near Water)

q: Before working over non-grounded ice:
o: Conduct an assessment that work can proceed safely
why: Non-grounded ice gets an assessment first - it is floating cover, not ground. (ASH - Working Over or Near Water)

q: Ice on a walkway gets:
why: Passageways stay clean, unobstructed, and free of ice or treated to prevent slipping injuries. (ASH - Housekeeping)

q: Electronic cigarettes on a process facility:
why: E-cigs follow the smoking policy: designated areas only. Production, process, drilling, and construction areas are no-smoking. (ASH - Smoking)

q: Who may repair, install, or adjust electrical equipment?
why: Qualified and authorized - both words. (ASH - Electrical)

q: How close may a non-electrician bring a conductive object to unguarded energized overhead lines?
o: Contact is fine if de-energized downstream
why: Only a qualified electrician may bring a conductive object closer than 15 feet to unguarded, energized overhead or un-insulated feeder lines. (ASH - Electrical)

q: Work directly on energized circuits rated 480/277 volts or greater requires:
why: Two qualified electrical persons for energized work at 480/277V or greater. Diagnostics under 600V may be one qualified person. (ASH - Electrical / Fired Heater Standard)

q: Using steam to purge a flammable atmosphere from process equipment requires:
o: A written specific procedure reviewed by Engineering and a Safety Representative
why: Each steam cleaning or purging application gets its own written procedure, reviewed by Engineering and Company Safety. (ASH - Steam Hazards)

q: Straight ladders must have:
why: Ensure straight ladders have safety feet - part of the pre-use inspection. (ASH - Ladder Safety)

q: Reaching from a ladder, the ASH limit is:
o: Keep your belt buckle between the rails
why: Belt buckle between the rails. If you cannot, move the ladder. (ASH - Ladder Safety)

q: Working from a ladder at 6 feet or greater:
why: At 6 feet or greater from a ladder, fall protection when feasible - the 6-foot line follows you onto the ladder. (ASH - Ladder Safety / Tool Usage)

q: Before using a pneumatic tool:
o: Inspect couplings, hoses, and connections - every use
why: Couplings, hoses, and connections get inspected each time - attached and secured. (ASH - Tool Usage)

q: Before putting the chuck key to an electric drill:
o: Disconnect it from its power source
Ask a second hand to steady it
why: Disconnect electric and air tools from power for chuck-key work and when not in use; pull battery packs from portables. (ASH - Tool Usage)

q: A powered hand tool with a trigger lock must release by:
o: Depressing the trigger itself - spring-loaded release
why: The lock releases by depressing the control switch or trigger. A separate positive on/off switch is prohibited. (ASH - Tool Usage)

q: A shop-made tool can be used when:
o: A qualified engineer approved it and no commercial tool exists
why: Field-fabricated or modified tools take qualified engineer approval, and only when no commercial option serves. (ASH - Tool Usage)

q: The ASH's position on open-blade knives:
o: Rarely the most appropriate cutting tool - evaluate each task
why: Rarely the right selection. Each work group evaluates cutting tasks and provides the safest tool. (ASH - Cutting Tools)

q: Camlock fittings in steam service:
why: Cam and groove fittings shall not be used for steam service - no configuration makes it acceptable. (ASH - Camlocks)

q: Before disconnecting a camlock in pressurized service:
o: Verify atmospheric pressure via bleeder valve or vent
Stand to the side and pull
why: A method of verifying atmospheric pressure - bleeder or vent - comes before disconnecting. Locked and secured while in service. (ASH - Camlocks)

q: Whip checks are typically rated for:
why: Typically under 200 psi - above that, whip checks alone are not the restraint answer. Pressurized transfer hoses get positively secured at ALL connection points. (ASH - Hose Restraints)

q: A scaffold may be used when:
o: It is tagged Ready For Use for that day
why: Only a scaffold tagged Ready For Use that day - inspected by a competent person before each shift and after anything that could affect integrity. (ASH - Scaffolds)

q: Scaffolds are designed by ___ and erected under ___.
o: A qualified person / a competent person's supervision
why: Designed by a qualified person, constructed under a competent person's supervision - two different roles by definition. (ASH - Scaffolds)

q: Sheet metal is stored:
o: Leaned against a wall or column
On edge in racks or on sleepers
why: Never leaned against walls or columns - on edge, in racks or on sleepers. (ASH - Materials Storage)

q: Passengers in heavy equipment:
o: One rider allowed in the cab
Not allowed unless the equipment is designed to carry them
why: Seat belts always, and riders only in equipment designed for passengers. (ASH - Heavy Equipment)

q: Before using heavy equipment to make a lift, the operator:
o: Makes a complete functional check of the unit
why: Operators assure themselves the unit can operate safely with a complete functional check before any lift or load work. (ASH - Heavy Equipment)

q: Before any heavy-equipment backing operation, operator and spotter complete:
o: A 360-degree hazard assessment, front to back and top to bottom
A path walk by the operator alone
why: Both of them, together: full 360 assessment of the proposed travel path for obstructions and energies. (ASH - Spotter Guidelines)

q: A designated spotter must be:
o: Trained in spotter responsibilities and proficient in hand signals
why: Trained and proficient in the designated hand signals, refreshed on competency or procedure change - and highly visible. (ASH - Spotter Responsibilities)

q: Before the lift, who determines load weight, center of gravity, and attachment points?
why: A competent person determines weight, CG, and best attachment before any lift is made. (ASH - Rigging/Lifting)

q: The capacity of a lift is set by:
o: The weakest link in the load path
why: Never exceed the weakest link - hoist, sling, shackle, turnbuckle, or eyebolt. The chain is the weakest part, not the strongest. (ASH - Rigging/Lifting)

q: A bridle sling with four legs is rated assuming:
o: Only TWO legs carry the load
why: Three or more legs: assume the load rides on two. The others are balance, not capacity. (ASH - Rigging/Lifting)

q: To shorten a chain sling you may:
o: Neither - never knot, bolt, or weld-repair slings
why: No knots in slings, no bolts between links, no welding repairs - shortening hardware or a different sling, nothing else. (ASH - Rigging/Lifting)

q: Flattening the sling angle toward horizontal:
why: Decreasing the angle between sling and horizontal INCREASES the stress in the legs - flat slings work hardest. (ASH - Rigging/Lifting)

q: A lift exclusion zone must be:
o: Clearly marked and actively monitored by a competent person
why: Marked, established before the lift, and actively monitored so nobody drifts in. (ASH - Rigging/Lifting)

q: Before moving a gas cylinder:
o: Close the valve; use a cart or get help
why: Valves closed before moving. Regulators come off and caps go on unless it rides a special hand truck secured. (ASH - Cylinder Handling)

q: Fuel gas cylinders are used:
why: Upright, secured against movement - always. (ASH - Cylinder Use)

q: Oxygen cylinders are stored how far from fuel gas cylinders?
o: 20 feet, or behind a 5-foot wall with a 30-minute fire rating
Same cage is fine if both are capped
why: 20 feet of separation, or a 5-foot barrier wall rated 30 minutes. Oxygen turns any fire into a fast one. (ASH - Cylinder Storage)

q: Which cylinder may enter a confined space?
why: Compressed gas cylinders stay out of confined spaces - except breathing air, fire extinguishers, and small aerosol cans like dye penetrant. (ASH - Cylinders / Confined Space)

q: Every oxy-acetylene torch rig requires:
o: Flashback arrestors at each regulator and check valves at each torch connection
why: Flashback arrestor on each regulator, check valve on each torch/hose connection - and nobody tampers with cylinder safety devices. (ASH - Cylinder Use)

q: Your air tool is dead and there's a nitrogen bottle right there. You:
o: Regulate it down and run the tool
Never use nitrogen in place of compressed air
Use it for under a minute
why: Never substitute nitrogen for compressed air. It works the tool fine and displaces the oxygen around your face. (ASH - Cylinders)

q: Before ordering a chemical new to the site:
o: Review the SDS and contact the Industrial Hygiene Department
why: SDS and New Chemical Review first, IH contacted before ordering. (ASH - Hazardous Materials)

q: Non-metal secondary containers for flammable liquids are:
o: Prohibited - except Nalgene up to 1 gallon for samples
why: Prohibited, with the narrow sampling exception - Nalgene to 1 gallon for samples and shakeouts. And every secondary container gets a HazCom label. (ASH - Flammable Liquids)

q: Before starting work with hazardous materials, you locate:
o: Safety showers, eyewash stations, and safety equipment
why: Know where the showers, eyewash, and safety equipment are BEFORE you need them - and keep a means of egress the whole time. (ASH - Hazardous Materials)

q: Approaching rig-move activity on a field road, slow to:
why: 5 mph approaching rig moves, no passing unless escort personnel direct it, and expect workers on the road. (ASH - Vehicle Safety)

q: Riding a snow machine or four-wheeler requires:
why: A helmet must be worn when traveling by four-wheeler or snow machine. (ASH - Transportation)

q: Phase I foul weather means:
o: Extreme-caution travel, equipment checked, arctic gear required
why: Phase I - Caution: field travel permitted with extreme caution, radios and lights verified working, arctic gear required. (ASH - Foul Weather)

q: Phase II foul weather requires:
o: Convoys of two or more vehicles with radio communication
why: Phase II - Restricted: convoy only, two-plus vehicles, radio comms between them. (ASH - Foul Weather)

q: Phase III foul weather permits:
o: Critical or emergency travel by heavy equipment convoy only
why: Phase III - Closed: heavy equipment convoy only, and only critical or emergency travel. (ASH - Foul Weather)

q: When foul weather is declared, supervisors must:
o: Post the phase on the board
Limit unnecessary vehicle traffic and notify their employees
why: Limit all unnecessary traffic and notify everyone who reports to them that foul weather conditions exist. (ASH - Foul Weather)

q: During helicopter operations, who is in complete charge?
why: The pilot is in complete charge of aircraft and passengers at all times, and gives the emergency briefing before flight. (ASH - Helicopter Travel)

q: You approach the rotor blade arc:
o: Only after the pilot signals it is safe
why: Not until the pilot signals. And the helipad stays clear until the aircraft has landed - it is not a staging area. (ASH - Helicopter Travel)

q: The ASH driving rules on fatigue:
o: Do not drive while fatigued or impaired
why: Do not drive while fatigued or impaired - full stop. Fatigue management is its own program for a reason. (ASH - Vehicle Safety / Fatigue)

q: The Issuing Authority on a permit is accountable for:
o: Ensuring the area and equipment are safe prior to starting work
why: Responsible for the area where work is permitted, accountable that area and equipment are safe before work starts. (ASH - Permits)

q: An Authorized Gas Tester is someone:
o: Authorized to use gas detection equipment for atmospheric testing
why: Authorized to use gas detection equipment for atmospheric testing purposes - a defined permit role, not just a monitor wearer. (ASH - Permits)

q: You cannot meet a safety standard on a job. The ASH route is:
o: The variance process - jobs should be structured to comply, variances are the exception
why: Structure the job to comply; a variance to a safety standard is a formal, documented exception - not a conversation. (ASH - Safe Work Expectations / Variance)

q: For a Defeated Safety Device, continuous operation is defined as:
o: Any 12-hour period from the time the system became inoperable
why: Any 12-hour period from when the system became inoperable - and jumpers impacting safety devices go on the DSD Log. (ASH - Defeated Safety Devices)

q: Your ground-disturbance work scope changes beyond the original ACWR description:
o: The process may have to start over
why: Scope changes outside the original project description can send the ACWR process back to the start. Dig what was cleared, nothing else. (ASH - Ground Disturbance)

q: Flame-resistant fired-heater ducting begins to degrade at:
why: Common flame-resistant flex duct degrades from 250 F - and duct contaminated with oil or flammables does not get used at all. (ASH - Fired Heater Standard)

q: A Tioga heater at 0 F ambient puts out roughly:
why: About 200 F outlet at 0 F ambient - and outlet climbs with ambient, so heating operations above 0 F get watched closely. (ASH - Fired Heater Standard)

q: Siting a mobile fired heater, wind is reviewed so that:
o: Potential hydrocarbon sources are downwind of the ignition source
why: Layout and prevailing wind get reviewed so hydrocarbon sources sit downwind of the ignition source - the wind carries vapors away from the flame, not to it. (ASH - Fired Heater Standard)

q: Mobile fired heater operations require what under the equipment?
o: Drip pans and/or surface liners per the spill prevention plan
why: Drip pans or liners per the Company spill prevention plan - a heater is an engine and a fuel system parked on your containment record. (ASH - Fired Heater Standard)

q: In an H2S designated area, personnel must:
why: Personal monitors in H2S designated areas - and the Unit Operator notes H2S potential on the permits. (ASH - H2S Standard)

q: A Process Safety Fundamental cannot be followed on your task. You:
o: Stop and discuss with your team and supervisor for a safe alternative
why: When a PSF cannot be followed: stop, have the discussion, and determine an alternative course to complete the work safely. (ASH - Process Safety Fundamentals)

q: Complete the ASH's opening rule: 'No job is so important that...'
o: ...you cannot take time to do it safely
why: No job is so important that you cannot take time to do it safely - the first line of the General Safety Rules. (ASH - General Safety Rules)

q: Heavy equipment is operated in accordance with:
why: Always per the manufacturer's operating instructions - the machine's book outranks habit. (ASH - Heavy Equipment)

q: Before manually lifting a load, the ASH says first:
o: Stretch and lift with your legs
Consider engineering or mechanical lifting methods, and determine the load's weight
why: Mechanical methods are the preferred control before manual handling - and make an effort to know the weight before you commit your back to it. (ASH - Material Lifting)

q: A spotter loses sight of hazards developing in the equipment's path. Their job is to:
o: Communicate observed hazards to the operator
why: Spotters communicate observed hazards to the operator - visibility and communication are the entire function. (ASH - Spotter Responsibilities)

q: Noise sign reads 82 dBA. You wear:
why: Over 82 dBA: hearing protection. Over 100 dBA: double - plugs AND muffs. The signs mark both thresholds. (ASH - Industrial Hygiene)
